persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Wanjiku, 21, a Kenyan student helping for one month at a church in Texas, USA. The church is filling shoeboxes with gifts for children (a project of an American charity that sends gift boxes to children in other countries, including Kenya). Bags of gifts are arriving, and the pastor asks you: how many complete boxes can we pack, and what do we still need?

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Shoebox Counter. You have never seen it before, and that is fine. In about four minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.

First, what is a shoebox drive? It is a project of an American charity. Churches in America fill shoeboxes with small gifts, like a toothbrush, a notebook, pencils and a toy. The boxes are sent to children in other countries. Some of them come to Kenya.
Now the problem. People bring many things to the church. Bags of crayons, socks, toothbrushes. Nobody knows how many full boxes that makes.
Here is the key idea. A box is only complete if it has one of every important thing. If you have ninety toothbrushes but only four notebooks, you can pack only four complete boxes, not ninety.
This app counts what comes in, and does that maths for you. It works for any collection: a food drive, a school supplies drive, a coat drive.
Who uses it? The person at a church who collects the gifts. In Kenya you could use it to collect school kits or food parcels.

lines.t: Let us look at the screen. At the top is the big number, Complete sets, right now. This is how many full boxes you can pack today. Below it, in red, the app tells you which item runs out first.
Next is the drive's goal: how many boxes you want to make. Tap the box and type a number.

Below that is a long list called Everything, A to Z. Each item has a count. To add things, type how many in the small box that says how many, then tap the plus button. If the box is empty, plus adds just one. The minus button takes away.

lines: You can also tap the number itself. A box opens that asks, How many came in? Type a number and tap Add them. If some were broken, tap Took some out. If you counted again, tap Fix the total.

Now tap the name of an item. A box opens with more choices. Goes in every set means every box needs this item, so it counts for the big number. We have plenty means you have so many that you do not need to count it any more.
In that box you can also type an exact count and tap Set, or tap Remove this item. Tap Done to close.

lines.t: To add a new item, scroll down to the box that says add an item, type a name, and tap Add.
The green button, Send the group what we still need, writes a message listing everything still missing. You can send it to your church group as a text.

lines: The line called What is not allowed any more lists things that must not go in a box, like soap, toothpaste and sweets.
The money shown is dollars, because it is American. Everything stays on this phone.
To start again, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap Start fresh, erase this app's data. It asks you twice.
In the test, you will collect gifts for a shoebox drive. Take your time, and if something is confusing, say so. Confusing parts are exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Wanjiku at the church in Texas. The counts are all zero. Nobody will tell you which button to press — use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Shoebox Counter with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. Every count is now 0 and the goal shows 100. (Do not use '↻ start a new drive' — it keeps the goal and any items you added.) (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this, even on a phone that still holds the old OCC Box Counter's shared count.)
challenge.challengeNote: Shared key: the retired OCC Box Counter saved under 'occ_counter_v1'. This app now saves only 'church_drive_v1' and copies occ_counter_v1 across once, on its very first open (guarded by the flag 'dj_drive_own_save'). The house Start fresh deliberately never erases occ_counter_v1 (house.py marks it shared), but it does erase church_drive_v1, and the dj_ flag survives, so the old count is NOT copied back in after Start fresh. The checks read church_drive_v1 only, so leftover OCC data can never make a task pass. Verified live by seeding occ_counter_v1 before first open.

tasks.text: Your church wants to pack 40 boxes this year. Tell the app.
tasks.hint: Look for the drive's goal near the top, under the big number.

tasks.text: Mrs Johnson brought 25 toothbrushes. Count them in.
tasks.hint: Find Toothbrushes in the list. Type the number in its small box and tap ＋, or tap its count.

tasks.text: 40 packs of crayons came in. Later you found that 4 packs were broken and threw them away. Make the count right.
tasks.hint: Crayons should end at 36. Tap its count: there is a way to take some out.

tasks.text: Your church decided every box must also have a jump rope. Jump ropes are not on the list. Add them, make them count for every box, and count in the 12 that came today.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('church_drive_v1')||'null');if(!d||!Array.isArray(d.items))return false;var f=function(s){return d.items.filter(function(i){return String(i.n||'').toLowerCase().indexOf(s)>=0})[0]};var i=f('jump rope')||f('jumprope')||f('skipping rope');return !!i&&!!i.box&&!i.plenty&&parseFloat(i.q)===12;}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Add the item at the bottom of the list, then tap its NAME — one switch says it goes in every set.

tasks.text: Someone gave so many tennis balls that you will never run out. Tell the app to stop counting them.
tasks.hint: Tap the name 'Balls/ tennis and other' and look for 'We have plenty'.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: counts the gifts that come in for a collection drive
tells you how many complete boxes you can pack, limited by the item that runs out first
shows what you still need, so you can ask people for it

daily.task: Add one packed box in the Shoebox Counter, or change one count.

explore.name: 🎯 Goal & the big number
explore.find: Open the Shoebox Counter. The top card.
explore.try: Type a goal. Try 0, letters and 99999. Watch the big number and the red line.

explore.name: 💬 Message to your group
explore.try: Change some words. Look at 💬 Text it, ✉️ Email it and 📋 Copy — don’t send. Tap the green button again to close.

explore.name: 📦 Drop-off · shipping · not allowed
explore.try: Read them. Open “What is not allowed any more”.

explore.name: ➕ The item rows
explore.try: Tap ＋ and − on a few items. Type 24 in the how-many box, then ＋.

explore.name: 🔢 Tap the number
explore.find: Tap the number in the middle of a row.
explore.try: Try a quick number, Add them, Took some out, Fix the total and Cancel.

explore.name: 📄 An item’s page
explore.try: Try ±5 and ±10, type a count and Set. Tick “Goes in every set” and “We have plenty”. Remove one item. Done.

explore.name: 🆕 Your own item · new drive
explore.find: At the bottom of the list.
explore.try: Add an item with a long name. Look at Start a new drive — it asks first.

explore.name: 🖨 Top buttons
explore.try: Tap 🖨 Print (cancel), 🎨 Look and Aa Size. Put them back after.

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open every line in it: Aa (size), ✨ Ask an AI, 🌉 More from Daraja, 🎬 Take the tour again. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
